List every completed, affirmative well-operation fact that the supplied text states and that fits one of the listed relations. Reports usually state several such facts, often more than one per sentence; a fact stated in passing or inside a longer clause still counts. Use the text alone. Return only a JSON array of objects with the string keys "subject", "relation", and "object"; return [] only when the text states no completed operation, depth, size, pressure, volume, date or status at all. Do not add explanations or markdown.

Rules:
- Choose relation names exactly from the supplied list of 21 definitions. Do not invent relations.
- Copy the subject as an exact text span. Use "well" for the report's own well only when no other subject is named; never attach another named well's facts to it.
- Copy the object as an exact substring, including written units and depth references. Do not normalize, convert, expand shorthand, supply missing units, or invent dates or status codes.
- Emit one fact per stated value. A paired depth such as 13243' MD/12625' TVD gives two facts, with objects "13243' MD" and "12625' TVD". Keep a stated interval as one interval object. A low and a high test pressure are two facts.
- A tubular written with its outside diameter, such as a 7" liner, also gives a casing_size fact whose object is the diameter as written. A composite hole size such as 8-1/2" x 9-7/8" is not a tubular diameter.
- A status that the text states as the well's state (such as "the well is temporarily abandoned", "the well has been TA'd", "well shut in", "plugged back to sidetrack", or a code such as TA, PA, COM, ST, BP, SI) gives a has_well_status fact; copy the status words as written. "Recompleted to" or "completed in" a named zone is a completed_in fact whose object is the zone, not a has_well_status fact.
- Numbers in names such as BN 7300' Sand are part of the name, not depths.
- Leave out only operations that the text calls planned, proposed, scheduled, approved or not done, operations that were attempted (tried, with an unclear or failed outcome), and facts whose wording is unclear to you.
- Distinguish total depth of the well from intermediate or section drilling depth. Distinguish cement plugs from cement behind casing and equipment setting from plug setting.
- Use tested_to_pressure only for a stated pressure test, not operating, pumping, injection, or bleed pressure. A pressure-test # is not the weight # in a tubular specification.
- Do not treat tool movements as drilling or setting. Use corrected values when a correction is explicitly stated. For mud weight changed from one value to another, extract the new weight.
- Keep names of zones, rigs, fluids and companies as written. A company performing work is not necessarily the well's operator. A date stays as written without borrowing a year from elsewhere.

Invented example 1:
Text: Ran 7" liner to 9,120 ft MD and tested the liner top to 1,000 psi; good test.
Output: [{"subject":"7\" liner","relation":"set_casing_at","object":"9,120 ft MD"},{"subject":"7\" liner","relation":"casing_size","object":"7\""},{"subject":"liner top","relation":"tested_to_pressure","object":"1,000 psi"}]

Output: [{"subject":"cement retainer","relation":"set_equipment_at","object":"3,410'"},{"subject":"brine","relation":"pumped","object":"40 bbls"},{"subject":"well","relation":"has_well_status","object":"temporarily abandoned"}]

Invented example 3:
Text: Perforated the K-2 sand from 5,200' to 5,230' on 4/12/2015. Plan to set a plug next month.
Output: [{"subject":"K-2 sand","relation":"perforated_interval","object":"5,200' to 5,230'"}]

Allowed relations:
spudded_on: The subject well was spudded (drilling started) on the object date.
reached_td: The subject well reached its total depth (TD) at the object depth.
drilled_to: The subject well was drilled to the object depth (an intermediate or section depth, including "section TD").
set_casing_at: The subject casing, liner or conductor was set, landed or run to the object depth (shoe or setting depth).
casing_size: The subject tubular has the object outside diameter.
casing_spec: The subject tubular has the object weight and/or grade (e.g. "23 lb/ft P-110").
cemented_interval: Cement was placed behind or in the subject over the object interval, or its top of cement (TOC) is at the object depth.
set_plug_at: The subject plug was set or placed at the object depth or over the object interval.
set_equipment_at: The subject packer, nipple, valve, tubing stop, hanger or retainer was set or is located at the object depth.
tagged_at: A tool tagged the subject (plug, TOC, fill, fish, obstruction) at the object depth.
cut_at: The subject was cut (and possibly pulled) at the object depth (often BML).
tested_to_pressure: The subject was pressure-tested to the object pressure.
fit_lot_emw: A formation integrity or leak-off test of the subject well held the object equivalent mud weight.
perforated_interval: The subject (well, tubing string, or zone) was perforated over the object interval.
has_mud_weight: The subject well's mud/fluid weight was (raised, reduced or displaced) to the object density.
completed_in: The subject well was completed or recompleted in the object zone.
encountered_marker: The subject well encountered (logged, penetrated) the object geologic marker or formation.
has_well_status: The subject well has or entered the object status (TA, PA, COM, ST, BP, SI).
used_rig: Operations on the subject well used the object rig or vessel.
operated_by: The subject well is operated by the object company (stated as operator, not a service company).
pumped: The object volume of the subject fluid was pumped or mixed and pumped.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Romany Love is a 1931 British musical film directed by Fred Paul and starring Esmond Knight, Florence McHugh and Roy Travers.
Triples: [['Romany Love', 'publication date', '1931'], ['Romany Love', 'genre', 'musical film'], ['Romany Love', 'director', 'Fred Paul'], ['Romany Love', 'cast member', 'Esmond Knight']]
Relations: ['publication date', 'genre', 'director', 'cast member']
Answer: 
publication date: The subject entity was published or released on the date specified by the object entity.
genre: The subject entity belongs to the genre specified by the object entity.
director: The subject entity was directed by the person or entity specified by the object entity.
cast member: The subject entity includes the person specified by the object entity as a member of its cast.

Example 2:
Text: Monopoly Star Wars is the 1997 Monopoly franchise Star Wars video game based on the board game and set in the Star Wars fictional universe.
Triples: [['Monopoly Star Wars', 'publication date', '1997'], ['Monopoly Star Wars', 'genre', 'Monopoly'], ['Monopoly Star Wars', 'media franchise', 'Star Wars'], ['Monopoly Star Wars', 'instance of', 'video game']]
Relations: ['publication date', 'genre', 'media franchise', 'instance of']
Answer:
publication date: The subject entity was published or released on the date specified by the object entity.
genre: The subject entity belongs to the genre specified by the object entity.
media franchise: The subject entity is a part of the media franchise specified by the object entity.
instance of: The subject entity is an instance or example of the type specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Josef Schäffer (born July 2, 1891 in Moravia) was an Austrian track and field athlete who competed in the 1912 Summer Olympics.
Triples: [['Josef Schäffer', 'date of birth', 'July 2, 1891'], ['Josef Schäffer', 'place of birth', 'Moravia'], ['Josef Schäffer', 'participant in', '1912 Summer Olympics'], ['1912 Summer Olympics', 'point in time', '1912']]
Relations: ['date of birth', 'place of birth', 'participant in', 'point in time']
Answer:
date of birth: The subject entity was born on the date specified by the object entity.
place of birth: The subject entity was born in the location specified by the object entity.
participant in: The subject entity took part in the event specified by the object entity.
point in time: The object entity specifies a specific point in time the subject entity took place in.

Example 4:
Text: Sam Cross (born 26 August 1992) is a Welsh rugby union player who plays for Wales and club rugby for the Ospreys as a flanker.
Triples: [['Sam Cross', 'date of birth', '26 August 1992'], ['Sam Cross', 'position played on team / speciality', 'flanker'], ['Ospreys', 'sport', 'rugby union'], ['flanker', 'part of', 'rugby union']]
Relations: ['date of birth', 'position played on team / speciality', 'sport', 'part of']
Answer:
date of birth: The subject entity was born on the date specified by the object entity.
position played on team / speciality: The subject entity plays the specified position or has the specified speciality on the team.
sport: The subject entity is associated with the sport specified by the object entity.
part of: The subject entity is a part of or belongs to the object entity.

Example 5:
Text: Ondel-ondel is a large puppet figure featured in Betawi folk performance of Jakarta, Indonesia.
Triples: [['Betawi', 'location', 'Jakarta'], ['Jakarta', 'country', 'Indonesia'], ['Indonesia', 'ethnic group', 'Betawi'], ['Indonesia', 'contains administrative territorial entity', 'Jakarta']]
Relations: ['location', 'country', 'ethnic group', 'contains administrative territorial entity']
Answer:
location: The subject entity is located in the place specified by the object entity.
country: The subject entity is located in the country specified by the object entity.
ethnic group: The subject entity contains the ethnic group specified by the object entity.
contains administrative territorial entity: The subject entity contains the administrative territorial entity specified by the object entity.

Example 6:
Text: George M. Coombs (November 27, 1851 – March 27, 1909) was an American architect from Maine.
Triples: [['George M. Coombs', 'date of birth', 'November 27, 1851'], ['George M. Coombs', 'date of death', 'March 27, 1909'], ['American', 'contains administrative territorial entity', 'Maine'], ['Maine', 'country', 'American']]
Relations: ['date of birth', 'date of death', 'contains administrative territorial entity', 'country']
Answer:
date of birth: The subject entity was born on the date specified by the object entity.
date of death: The subject entity died on the date specified by the object entity.
contains administrative territorial entity: The subject entity contains or is a part of the administrative territorial entity specified by the object entity.
country: The subject entity is located in the country specified by the object entity.

Text:
Stone has successfully completed zone change operations on the SS 112 V-4 well to produce the "R-14" sand. The previous completion, the "C-2" sand, was isolated by setting a CIBP @ 11,163' MD and dumping 50' of cmt on top of the CIBP, w/ ETOC @ 11,113' MD. The "R-14" sand was exposed to production by perforating the intervals 10,870'-10,880' MD, 10,918'-10,930' MD, & 10,938'-10.950' MD. Operations began on 09/29/2010 and ended 10/18/2010.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Romany Love is a 1931 British musical film directed by Fred Paul and starring Esmond Knight, Florence McHugh and Roy Travers.
Triples: [['Romany Love', 'publication date', '1931'], ['Romany Love', 'genre', 'musical film'], ['Romany Love', 'director', 'Fred Paul'], ['Romany Love', 'cast member', 'Esmond Knight']]
Relations: ['publication date', 'genre', 'director', 'cast member']
Answer: 
publication date: The subject entity was published or released on the date specified by the object entity.
genre: The subject entity belongs to the genre specified by the object entity.
director: The subject entity was directed by the person or entity specified by the object entity.

Rules:
- Choose relation names exactly from the supplied list of 21 definitions. Do not invent relations.
- Copy the subject as an exact text span. Use "well" for the report's own well only when no other subject is named; never attach another named well's facts to it.

- A tubular written with its outside diameter, such as a 7" liner, also gives a casing_size fact whose object is the diameter as written. A composite hole size such as 8-1/2" x 9-7/8" is not a tubular diameter.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Romany Love is a 1931 British musical film directed by Fred Paul and starring Esmond Knight, Florence McHugh and Roy Travers.
Triples: [['Romany Love', 'publication date', '1931'], ['Romany Love', 'genre', 'musical film'], ['Romany Love', 'director', 'Fred Paul'], ['Romany Love', 'cast member', 'Esmond Knight']]
Relations: ['publication date', 'genre', 'director', 'cast member']
Answer: 
publication date: The subject entity was published or released on the date specified by the object entity.
genre: The subject entity belongs to the genre specified by the object entity.
director: The subject entity was directed by the person or entity specified by the object entity.
cast member: The subject entity includes the person specified by the object entity as a member of its cast.

Example 2:
Text: Monopoly Star Wars is the 1997 Monopoly franchise Star Wars video game based on the board game and set in the Star Wars fictional universe.

Text:
Per the approved APM, Anadarko permitted to attempt to open the XRFV in the Amp 2 Lower, flow test the Amp 2 Lower, and then change to the Amp 2 Upper. Anadarko was able to achieve a successful negative test. Anadarko is currently only producing the Amp 2 Upper.

Anadarko set the optional pump-thru plug in the XRFV to isolate the Amp 2 Lower. The plug was set above the Amp 2 Lower mechanical sleeve. The sleeve for the Amp 2 Lower is a Superior X-Radial Flow Valve. Anadarko achieved a successful test on the plug, so we know the Amp 2 Lower is isolated. 

First we ran a check set tool that showed the plug was actually set. Then we performed the negative test by pulling > 500 psi off the plug and holding.

Since Anadarko has the lower frac pack isolated via plug and the successful negative test, then a commingling application has not been submitted to date. Should Anadarko decide to produce both the Amp 2 Lower and Amp 2 Upper in the future, then BSEE-Rate Control would be consulted prior to doing so.

Per the approved APM, Anadarko permitted to attempt to open the XRFV in the Amp 2 Lower, flow test the Amp 2 Lower, and then change to the Amp 2 Upper. Anadarko was able to achieve a successful negative test. Anadarko is currently only producing the Amp 2 Upper.

Anadarko set the optional pump-thru plug in the XRFV to isolate the Amp 2 Lower. The plug was set above the Amp 2 Lower mechanical sleeve. The sleeve for the Amp 2 Lower is a Superior X-Radial Flow Valve. Anadarko achieved a successful test on the plug, so we know the Amp 2 Lower is isolated. 

First we ran a check set tool that showed the plug was actually set. Then we performed the negative test by pulling > 500 psi off the plug and holding.

Since Anadarko has the lower frac pack isolated via plug and the successful negative test, then a commingling application has not been submitted to date. Should Anadarko decide to produce both the Amp 2 Lower and Amp 2 Upper in the future, then BSEE-Rate Control would be consulted prior to doing so.

Rigged up the Pride 1502 rig on slot 7 EB 161 A-13.  TIH w/ 13-1/2" directional BHA, washed out the drive pipe with 8.6 ppg seawater and surveyed.  Directionally drilled w/ 13-1/2" BHA to 2,890' MD. Displace seawater to 10.8 ppg SBM and drilled out shoe track and 10? of new formation and ran LOT to 11.9 ppg.  Slide drilled to 5,964' MD.  Ran 7-3/4" casing tagging up at 5,219? MD.  Unable to get deeper.  Cemented in place in 2 stages with the ICP/stage collar and set on back-ups slips in the wellhead at the surface.  P/U 6-1/2? x 7-1/2" BHA and drilled out cement and 10? new formation and ran LOT to 13.6 ppg which was not sufficient to get to TD.  Performed first EZ Squeeze at the 7-3/4? casing shoe.  Drilled to 6,162? MD and had losses that prevented further drilling.  Performed second EZ Squeeze across entire open hole section and again had losses that prevented drilling ahead.  Set two expandable liners, the second of which was successfully set at 6,162? MD.  Directionally drilled with 5-1/2? x 6-1/2? BHA to TD of 7,230' MD.  Ran and cemented 5" liner due to the smaller hole restriction.  Circulated 12.3 ppg SBM in the hole.  ND BOPE and installed dry hole tree and tested to 1,000 psi.  Skidded rig to slot 6 for A-1ST.

Reports usually state several such facts, often more than one per sentence; a fact stated in passing or inside a longer clause still counts. Use the text alone. Return only a JSON array of objects with the string keys "subject", "relation", and "object"; return [] only when the text states no completed operation, depth, size, pressure, volume, date or status at all. Do not add explanations or markdown.

Rules:
- Choose relation names exactly from the supplied list of 21 definitions. Do not invent relations.
- Copy the subject as an exact text span. Use "well" for the report's own well only when no other subject is named; never attach another named well's facts to it.
- Copy the object as an exact substring, including written units and depth references. Do not normalize, convert, expand shorthand, supply missing units, or invent dates or status codes.
- Emit one fact per stated value. A paired depth such as 13243' MD/12625' TVD gives two facts, with objects "13243' MD" and "12625' TVD". Keep a stated interval as one interval object. A low and a high test pressure are two facts.
- A tubular written with its outside diameter, such as a 7" liner, also gives a casing_size fact whose object is the diameter as written. A composite hole size such as 8-1/2" x 9-7/8" is not a tubular diameter.
- A status that the text states as the well's state (such as "the well is temporarily abandoned", "the well has been TA'd", "well shut in", "plugged back to sidetrack", or a code such as TA, PA, COM, ST, BP, SI) gives a has_well_status fact; copy the status words as written. "Recompleted to" or "completed in" a named zone is a completed_in fact whose object is the zone, not a has_well_status fact.
- Numbers in names such as BN 7300' Sand are part of the name, not depths.
- Leave out only operations that the text calls planned, proposed, scheduled, approved or not done, operations that were attempted (tried, with an unclear or failed outcome), and facts whose wording is unclear to you.
- Distinguish total depth of the well from intermediate or section drilling depth. Distinguish cement plugs from cement behind casing and equipment setting from plug setting.
- Use tested_to_pressure only for a stated pressure test, not operating, pumping, injection, or bleed pressure. A pressure-test # is not the weight # in a tubular specification.
- Do not treat tool movements as drilling or setting. Use corrected values when a correction is explicitly stated. For mud weight changed from one value to another, extract the new weight.
- Keep names of zones, rigs, fluids and companies as written. A company performing work is not necessarily the well's operator. A date stays as written without borrowing a year from elsewhere.
